description: Probability that a parcel is built within 5 years, given feasim's profit ratio R = value of the new project / (construction and soft costs + the parcel's current assessed land value + its current assessed building value). R = 1 is break-even. See README.md.

existing_house_curve.formula: P5 = 1 - (1 - 1/(1 + exp(-z)))^5, z = const + lnR*ln(R) + own*owner_occupied + lnbl*ln(B/L) + steep*steep + tsunami_extreme*extreme_tsunami_zone + slr32*sea_level_rise_3.2ft_zone  (z is the log-odds of the annual probability of a new-home permit)

terms.R: profit ratio (see description). Construction cost is $150 per sq ft in late-2021 dollars, scaled by the construction materials price index (FRED WPUSI012011) to the valuation date
terms.ln(B/L): assessed building value / land value; typical Oahu lot 0.285 (2025 roll)
terms.steep: slope of 20% or more at the lot centroid, from USGS 10 m elevation data (11.5% of Oahu lots)
terms.extreme_tsunami_zone: extreme tsunami evacuation zone (Hawaii Statewide GIS hazard layer 12)
terms.sea_level_rise_3.2ft_zone: area exposed to the 1% annual chance coastal flood with 3.2 ft of sea-level rise (Hawaii Statewide GIS hazard layer 15)

existing_house_curve.held_out: Held out by years: fitted on 2017-2021, predicts 2022-2025 permits within -10% (517 vs 575); fitted on 2022-2025, predicts 2017-2021 within +15%. Leave-one-year-out: mean absolute error 25% for a single year. With construction cost held fixed instead of indexed, the same tests miss by +62% and -42%
existing_house_curve.fitted_on: Oahu single-family-zoned lots with an existing house, tax years 2017-2025: each year's assessed values (as of October 1 of the prior year) matched to new-home building permits issued that calendar year (1,050,343 lot-years, 120,172 lots, 1,468 permits; 2025 is January-June). Assessed values for 2017-2021 come from UHERO's scraped assessor records
existing_house_curve.other_islands: borrowed from Oahu, because only Honolulu publishes parcel-level permits; Maui assessment data also show owner-occupied homes rebuilt less often; slope and hazard flags are available statewide
existing_house_curve.valid_range_R_note: range of R in the fitting data; values outside it are extrapolation
existing_house_curve.outcome: building permit issued. To count homes finished instead, multiply P5 by finished_per_permit_5yr
existing_house_curve.finished_per_permit_basis: Honolulu new-home permits (1-4 units) issued 2013-2019: 95.2% were closed out as finished; of those, 74% within 1.5 years and 95% within 4.5 years of issue. Permits spread evenly over five years leave 72.8% finished by the end of year five
existing_house_curve.previous_version: v1 (Nov 2026) was fitted on the 2022 roll and Jan 2022-Jun 2025 permits only, with cost held fixed: const -5.65, lnR 6.08, own -0.84, lnbl -0.31, steep -0.70, tsunami -0.32, slr -0.33. It failed the held-out-years test (-32 to -42%)
existing_house_curve.valid_range_note: 1st to 99th percentile of R in the fitting data; values outside it, including a 20% profit, are extrapolation

vacant_lot.formula: P5 = 1 - (1 - 1/(1 + exp(-(a_island + b*ln(R)))))^5  (the logistic term is the annual probability)

a_Kauai.basis: Kauai publishes no assessed values, so nothing was measured there. Central value is the average of Oahu, Maui and Hawaii County RS/RD; range spans those three. Building permits per resident were tested as a way to place Kauai among the islands but did not line up with the measured rates

vacant_lot.cost_rule: construction cost per sq ft set separately for each island so that its median vacant lot has R = 1 (Oahu $150, Maui $123, Hawaii County RS/RD $92, rural $38). Curves are comparable within an island, not across islands
vacant_lot.outcome: a new building recorded on a later assessment roll (Oahu 2022 to 2026, Maui 2020 to 2025, Hawaii County about Oct 2022 to 2026). Note this differs from the existing-house curve, which counts building permits
vacant_lot.tests: held out by plat across all four areas, one shared profit slope predicts better than a flat rate and as well as separate slopes per island; Maui alone is close to flat (44 builds)

developer_controlled_5yr.caution: these lots were identified by clusters of new homes in the same window, so the rate is biased upward by the construction itself. Prefer the approved-project rate, or count subdivisions by each project's own schedule

approved_project_5yr.basis: 13 projects approved by the Honolulu City Council under HRS 201H in 2019-21 (DPP status report, Feb 2024): share with a building permit 3-4 years later. Oahu only; borrowed for other islands. Of 13 approved in 2022-24, 1 had a permit by Feb 2024, which is too soon to measure
approved_project_5yr.outcome_note: building permit issued, not finished. Buildings of 100+ units took a median of 30 months from permit to completion (Honolulu, 2005-2019), so on a finished-homes basis the five-year share would be lower; not yet converted

market_conditions_multiplier.basis: The house curve now pools 2017-2025 and its profit term follows construction costs, so no shift is applied by default. Low end: the weakest five-year stretch of 2017-2025 relative to the model (0.88, from leave-one-year-out ratios of observed to predicted permits). High end: Oahu rebuilding in 2005-2025 ran up to 1.25 times the 2017-2025 average in its 90th-percentile five-year window, a period the assessed values do not cover

not_covered: apartment and commercial zones: no profit curve yet (see apartment_zones); the TOD, parking and fee scenarios currently use the single-family curves
which specific parcels get built: use expected units = sum of P5 x net new units

tested_and_rejected.house_built_since_2005: no improvement once profit is included
tested_and_rejected.lot_size: no improvement once profit is included
tested_and_rejected.FEMA_flood_zone: no effect on Oahu rebuilds (multiplier 0.93, worse held-out); none on vacant lots
tested_and_rejected.slope_on_vacant_lots: no held-out gain (land value already reflects it)
tested_and_rejected.lava_zones_Hawaii_County: lava hazard zones 1-2 and 3 slightly lower (0.88, 0.84) but the held-out improvement is marginal; not used
tested_and_rejected.high_fire_risk: vacant lots in high wildfire-risk areas are built more often (1.3x), which reflects where growth is (dry leeward areas), not fire risk; not used
tested_and_rejected.tsunami_all_zones: the all-zones tsunami layer covers nearly every lot, so it carries no information

definitions.plat: a group of neighboring parcels sharing the first five digits of Hawaii's tax map key (TMK) parcel number
definitions.developer subdivision: a plat (or, for the cross-island vacant-lot curves, a 400 m grid cell) with at least five new homes on vacant lots in the measurement window; for the cross-island curves its annual build rate must also be at least 5.6%. These lots are excluded from the vacant-lot curves and reported under developer_controlled_5yr
definitions.owner_occupied: parcel receives the homeowner property-tax exemption, which applies only to an owner's primary residence
definitions.Hawaii Co RS/RD: Hawaii County single-family and double-family residential zones (RS, RD)
definitions.Hawaii Co rural: Hawaii County residential-agricultural and small agricultural lots (RA, A-1a, A-3a)
definitions.201H: Hawaii Revised Statutes chapter 201H, which lets the County Council waive zoning and other requirements for housing projects with affordable units
definitions.P5: probability of being built within 5 years; the logistic function gives an annual probability, compounded over 5 years

apartment_zones.measured: Oahu apartment and business-zoned lots (single-record, privately assessed, 5,000 sq ft or more), tax years 2017-2025: 29 permits for buildings of 5+ units in 59,294 lot-years. Annual rate about 0.23% for vacant or parking lots (about 1.2% in five years), 0.05% where building value is under a quarter of land value, and 0.01-0.02% for more built-up lots
apartment_zones.held_out: Rates from 2017-2021 predicted 7 projects for 2022-2025 against 20 observed; rates from 2022-2025 predicted 26 for 2017-2021 against 9. Too few and too volatile to fit a profit curve
apartment_zones.note: These rates are not conditioned on feasibility. Many large Oahu projects are on multi-record or government land and are counted under approved_project_5yr instead. With feasim's per-parcel profit for these lots, a profit slope could be tested on the same 29 projects
